name: SensorKit research sensors
plain: Reads broad passive sensor data for approved research studies only.
meaning: Gives researchers keyboard metrics, ambient light, device usage and more over months, a deep behavioral record. Apple limits it to reviewed studies.

android.note: No equivalent third party research sensor API; Health Connect and Health Services cover fitness only

ios.prompt_ui: Per sensor consent sheet plus study description and privacy policy URL
ios.persistence: Data held 24 hours before app can read it
ios.revocation: Settings > Privacy & Security > Research Sensor & Usage Data
ios.store_policy: Apple approves IRB approved research studies only
ios.note: Raw data stays on device for 24 hours so people can delete it

fields.name: sensors
fields.range: ambient light, keyboard metrics, phone usage, visits, and others

limits.headline: Can't collect broad sensor data like research studies do, unless Apple approves a study
limits.user_action: You join an approved research study and approve each sensor on a consent sheet
can: Collect passive sensor data for an Apple approved research study on iPhone
Show a per sensor consent sheet with study details and privacy policy link
Keep raw data on device for 24 hours so you can delete it
cannot: Use it in a normal app; Apple must approve the study first
Exist on Android; Health Connect and Health Services cover fitness only
Collect a sensor you did not approve
Keep raw data on the phone past 24 hours
limits.differs: iPhone only, for approved studies. Android has no matching third party research sensor system.

story.what_it_is: Lets approved research apps read broad passive sensor data over months.

marketing.name: SensorKit
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: research apps can collect broad sensor data, with Apple review and clear consent from participants.

story.for_you: If you join a study, you see a clear consent screen. The research app can then read things like keyboard typing speed, light, phone use and movement for months. You can stop at any time.
story.for_makers: Researchers get rich, passive data without asking people to log it. Apple reviews each study first, so only approved research can use it.

use_cases.example: A mental health study tracks sleep and phone use to look for signs of depression.
A study of Parkinson's disease measures typing and movement for months.
A university tracks how screen time changes during exams.
A study links watch data and phone use to mood.
Privacy experts watch SensorKit to make sure it does not leak to ads.
Apple bans using SensorKit data for ads or sales.

story.android_note: Android has no matching research tool.
story.ios_note: Needs an Apple entitlement and study review, and is not open to ordinary apps.
